hero.title: Ola x Navier - India's electric-mobility pioneer, on the water
hero.subtitle: Ola Electric is driving India's EV transition. The water is the next clean surface.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch an Ola electric foiling water tier across India's densest coastal flows - Mumbai's harbour, Goa's coast, Kerala's backwaters and the Andaman islands - booked in-app, clean, category-defining. Navier brings the software-defined hydrofoiling fleet and the Maldives-proven playbook; Ola brings the demand, the app and an electric-mobility identity that fits the water perfectly.

why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, ~10x more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable and autonomy-ready - and all-electric on the Pioneer II, a direct fit for Ola Electric's brand. A ~100-vessel network is ramping in the Maldives next door; Kochi's electric Water Metro proves India's clean-ferry appetite; and India's busiest coastal flows run on diesel craft. The clean-water category gets claimed cluster-by-cluster.
multimodal_fit: Ola already runs real-time demand, dispatch, pricing and a vast driver-partner network across India. An electric foiling water tier slots straight in: same app, captain-partners on the water, the water leg booked door-to-door with the Ola ride to and from the jetty - and a clean story consistent end-to-end with Ola Electric.

differentiation.why_navier: All-electric (Pioneer II) and software-defined - a direct fit for the Ola Electric identity - with a factory in Turkey for supply and a ~100-vessel network already proving the model in the Maldives. The clean water tier is a category Ola can own.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. network_thesis.headline: One app. India's 7,500 km coastline. The clean-water layer of India's electric-mobility pioneer.
network_thesis.body: India is a coastline of harbours, tidal rivers, backwaters and island archipelagos - and no platform owns the water. Ola Electric gives Ola a clean-mobility identity that fits the water perfectly: the same all-electric foiling tier proven in the Maldives extends to Mumbai's harbour, Goa's coast, Kerala's backwaters and the Andaman islands. Pick one market to prove it, or roll the recommended sequence. The fleet, app integration and captain-partner model are identical everywhere.
network_thesis.how_to_read: Each card is a real, ready market. Start with Mumbai - Ola's flagship metro and the harbour with the most proven water demand - or pick any cluster. The phased sequence below is our recommended path.
network_thesis.coverage_note: Ola is India's home-grown mobility pioneer with a clean-mobility identity via Ola Electric; these four markets are where the coastal water demand is densest today. The same all-electric fleet and in-app tier extend to every harbour, river and island corridor Ola serves on land.

hero.what_we_do_together: Ola brings the in-app demand, the land first/last mile and a clean-mobility identity via Ola Electric; Navier brings the silent electric foiling fleet. Together we extend Ola's electric story onto Andaman & Nicobar Islands's water.

partner_context.their_ambition: Ola is extending its clean-mobility identity into India's high-growth tourism geographies.
partner_context.their_pressure: Andaman inter-island transport is captive to diesel ferries with no clean or premium tier.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: An electric foiling tier gives Ola a clean, ownable island-hopping product on India's busiest tropical archipelago - fitting its electric brand in coral-sensitive waters.

markets.why_now: Andaman tourism is booming on diesel ferries in coral-sensitive waters, the government is pushing connectivity, and Ola's electric identity fits a clean island tier.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: India's busiest island-hop sells out on diesel ferries in coral-sensitive waters - exactly where Ola's clean electric foiling tier is most differentiated.

proof_points.claim: Port Blair<->Havelock is India's busiest island-hop.
proof_points.evidence: ~38 nm on diesel fast-ferries that sell out in peak season - a captive, high-margin tourism corridor.

proof_points.claim: The star islands drive the demand.
proof_points.evidence: Havelock (Radhanagar Beach) and Neil are top domestic-honeymoon and diving destinations.

proof_points.claim: Coral-sensitive marine parks reward clean propulsion.
proof_points.evidence: The Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park and surrounding reefs make zero-wake foiling an environmental asset over diesel ferries.

proof_points.claim: Government is pushing Andaman connectivity.
proof_points.evidence: Central focus on island tourism and connectivity under Maritime India Vision 2030 provides a policy tailwind.

objections.concern: The islands are remote with limited infrastructure.
objections.response: Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at existing jetties; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all - ideal for remote-island operations.
Peak tourism is the calm Oct-May window; foils handle shoulder-season chop better than the diesel fast-ferries.
Marine-tourism operators already work within the A&N Administration's framework - we build on the established path.

end_state.headline: The water layer of the Andamans - India's island-hopping archipelago, in-app.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Port Blair + Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) + Neil (Shaheed Dweep) + Ross/North Bay/Baratang + North Andaman - India's Bay of Bengal tourism archipelago.
end_state.narrative: Starting from the Port Blair<->Havelock<->Neil spine, Ola makes the Andamans a first-class in-app island-hopping surface: silent foiling transfers replacing the diesel fast-ferries, clean reef day-trips, and a Quanta-LR North Andaman line-haul - bookable in the app travellers already use on the mainland.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet, captain training, the maintenance & certification path, and a uniform integration spec.
the_ask.partner_brings: Demand, the rider/guest relationship, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands as the launch market to prove the on-water tier.
the_ask.next_step: Scope a Phase-1 pilot (~3 vessels) on the entry corridor, building to ~59 vessels as the network matures (addressable ceiling ~147).

proof_points.claim: Ola owns a clean-mobility identity no rival can claim.
proof_points.evidence: Ola Cabs created India's ride-hail category, and Ola Electric is driving the country's EV transition across two- and four-wheelers. An electric foiling water tier is the natural extension of that clean-mobility brand onto the water.

proof_points.claim: The vessel is commercial today.
proof_points.evidence: The N30 Pioneer II is in commercial service now — 70 nm range, ~30 kt, 6–8 passengers — already operating with the Four Seasons on Lake Austin. Delivery-ready, all-electric, not a concept.

proof_points.claim: A network at scale is already being built in the region.
proof_points.evidence: Navier is ramping a roughly 100-vessel water network in the Maldives with JIH Global over three years and signed a national agreement with WorldBridge in Cambodia in May 2026 — South Asian and Southeast Asian proof the model scales.

proof_points.claim: Foiling is differentiated, electric, and hard for a road rival to copy.
proof_points.evidence: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water for dramatically lower energy per passenger-mile — an electric water tier that fits Ola's identity and that a road-only price war can't reach.

objections.concern: Ride-hail share has slipped — why add a new mode now?
objections.response: The road is exactly where the price war is. A clean, electric water tier is differentiated demand a rival can't undercut — and it plays to Ola Electric's identity rather than fighting Uber and Rapido on fares.

objections.concern: Is the range enough for India's coast?
objections.response: The dense commute and bay hops — Mumbai↔Alibaug ~11 nm, Panaji↔beaches ~14 nm — sit inside the all-electric Pioneer II envelope. The Quanta-LR hybrid reaches the Andamans and even Lakshadweep with no charging infrastructure required.
Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists — open water and the jetties already in use. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; launch doesn't wait on new ports.

objections.concern: Why boats for a mobility app?
objections.response: Ola brings demand, dispatch, the wallet and the brand; Navier brings the fleet, captains and maintenance — the same split that built Ola's road network, applied to India's 7,500 km of coast, backwaters and islands.

end_state.headline: The electric water layer of India's home-grown mobility pioneer.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every coastal and backwater market Ola already serves — Mumbai and the Konkan, Goa's rivers and coast, Kerala's Kochi and backwaters, and the Andaman & Nicobar islands.

steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II electric capillaries + Quanta-LR island legs
steady_state.tam_framing: Tens of millions of harbour, backwater and island trips a year, today lost to gridlock and timetables, moved into the Ola app.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is the coastal and backwater map of India. Start where the congestion is worst — Mumbai's harbour, Goa's rivers, Kochi's backwaters — prove the electric in-app water tier, then reach the Andamans and Lakshadweep.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined, all-electric foiling fleet (Pioneer II + Quanta-LR), captain training, maintenance and the network operating system.
the_ask.partner_brings: Demand and dispatch through the Ola app, the wallet, the clean-mobility brand, and the choice of launch city.
the_ask.next_step: Scope a first pilot in one flagship cluster — Mumbai or Kochi — co-defining the in-app electric water tier on three corridors.

close.title: India's electric-mobility pioneer — now on the water.
close.body: Ola made India's roads electric. Water is the next clean surface, and no road rival can follow there on price. Start in one harbour or backwater, prove the electric foiling tier, and extend it across India's coast.

revenue_potential.headline: The floor and the prize — every rung traces to grounded, sourced demand.
revenue_potential.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
revenue_potential.anchor_note: $14M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.

rungs.label: SOM — floor (published)
rungs.basis: sourced flagship corridors · 10% capture · today's demand

rungs.label: SOM — full network
rungs.basis: whole mapped network · 10% capture · today's demand (no growth assumed)

rungs.label: SAM — matured network
rungs.basis: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market · leading-operator 25% capture, network-wide

rungs.label: Marine mobility TAM — induced marine-transfer market
rungs.basis: SAM divided by leading-operator capture — the full inducible water-transfer wallet at network maturity

rungs.label: Journey GMV — food + stays + experiences (≈3× TAM)
rungs.basis: add food, stays, and experiences to every crossing in the induced market

rungs.label: Partner platform revenue on Navier
rungs.basis: platform commission on journey GMV routed through the Navier network (subset of full Journey GMV)

ceiling_sibling.label: Platform revenue ceiling — 18% × full Journey GMV
ceiling_sibling.derivation: journey_gmv.mid × 0.18 (full GMV ceiling, not Navier-corridor subset)
ceiling_sibling._doc: Sibling reference. Do NOT promote to a 7th ladder rung. Platform_rev rung remains the Navier-subset Interpretation-A value.

phase_economics.headline: Revenue potential by phase — conservative floor first, ecosystem prize last.
phase_economics.conversion_note: Fleet & CO2 scale from the grounded unit: 15 boats = $1M transport rev = 450 t CO2/yr (~$96K rev/boat).

vessel_sizing.headline: Right vessel for every leg — corridor range picks the hull.

classes.role: Capillary corridors ≤ 70nm. The workhorse of Prove + Scale.
Doubles throughput per hull on dense corridors; roughly halves payback. Scale-phase workhorse.
Regional legs 75–150nm beyond Pioneer range. Held out of near-term numbers.

vessel_sizing.range_gate_note: ≤ 70nm → Pioneer II (now). 75–150nm → Quanta-LR (roadmap). Long legs never faked on a 70nm boat.

_render_chip_flag.confidence_display: Tag every banded rung; lead with floor + corridor COUNT (ID-traceable). Never headline the 'high' band.

growth_case.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
growth_case.modal_headline: Floor to prize — every rung traces to grounded demand

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.

ladder_transitions.headline: Ola platform take on Navier-carried journeys
ladder_transitions.basis: Platform-take step. Platform commission applied to the journey GMV routed through the Navier network (Navier-captured subset, not the full induced market).
ladder_transitions._lb_ref: LB-113: partner_platform_rev_on_navier = on-Navier subset, distinct from deck's '18% × full Journey GMV' narrative ceiling
